question.worked_solution:
First, we note that $x=0$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

We multiply both sides of the equation by $2x,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-2}{2x}+\frac{x-4}{2x} & =\frac{5x-6}{2x} \\ 2x\cdot (\frac{x-2}{2x}+\frac{x-4}{2x}) & =n\cdot (\frac{5x-6}{2x}) \\ 2x\cdot \frac{x-2}{2x}+2x\cdot \frac{x-4}{2x} & =2x\cdot \frac{5x-6}{2x} \\ \cancel{2x}\cdot \frac{x-2}{\cancel{2x}}+\cancel{2x}\cdot \frac{x-4}{\cancel{2x}} & =\cancel{2x}\cdot \frac{5x-6}{\cancel{2x}} \\ x-2+x-4 & =5x-6\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $x,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2+x-4 & =5x-6 \\ 2x-6 & =5x-6 \\ 5x-2x & =-6+6 \\ 3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We recall that we cannot allow $x=0$ as a solution. Therefore, we conclude that there is no solution.
